task.title: Checking What References Changed Content
task.shortdesc: Before changing a reused element, topic, or key, use the References tab to list the maps and topics affected by the change.

keywords.indexterm: References tabchecking the effect of a change

prereq.p: The References tab must be enabled. On your Profile page, in the Preferences section, select Show the DITA References tab in the Explore side view.

context.p: Use this procedure to list the resources affected by a change:

step.cmd: Open the file that contains the content in the editor, then place the caret inside the element that you want to change.
step.info: For example, place it inside a warning that other topics reuse via a content reference.

step.stepresult: The Explore side view opens to the References tab and displays the file in the Referenced by direction. If other files reference elements in the file, the tab groups them by element and highlights the group that contains the element at the caret.

step.cmd: Review the files in the highlighted Element id group.
step.info: Each file in the group references the element. The number next to a file shows how many times that file references it.

step.cmd: To follow the references further, expand a file.
step.info: The file expands to display the files that reference it. For example, a topic expands to show the maps that include it, and a map expands to show the maps that include it, up to the root map of each publication.

step.cmd: To see only what one publication includes, select it as the context publication, then click Use the context publication as scope on the toolbar.
step.info: The tab then applies the publication's profiling and resolves keys as the publication does. See .

step.cmd: Click a file to open the referencing file in the editor, at the element that holds the reference.

result.p: You now have a list of files to check or update after making the change.

p.b: Example: What Does a Map Pull In?

result.p: To learn what a map includes, open it in the editor and click the References tab icon in the Explore side view. The tab starts at the root map of the active publication. To show another map, enter part of its name in the field at the top of the tab, then click References. The tab lists the topics, keys, maps, and images that the map references. Each file expands to show what it references.
